detailed_reviews.printed_core: Nonamenable case in full: (18.5) cited from 'the reasoning of the first paragraph of the proof of Theorem 6.19 and (6.37)'; defines kappa_n, lambda_n; rewrites (18.5) as 2/(d-dagger - |d_E L_n|/|L_n|) + 2/(d + |d_E K_n|/|K_n|) <= 1 + 1/|E(L_n)|; expands into kappa_n, lambda_n; derives 2 lambda_n <= ((d-dagger - Phi-dagger)^2/(d+Phi)) 2 kappa_n + (d-dagger - Phi-dagger)^2/|E(L_n)| and the symmetric 2 kappa_{n+1} bound; combines into 2 kappa_{n+1} <= a(2 kappa_n) + b_n with a = (((d-Phi)(d-dagger-Phi-dagger))/((d+Phi)(d-dagger+Phi-dagger)))^2 < 1 and b_n -> 0; concludes kappa_n -> 0 and lambda_n -> 0.

detailed_reviews.precise_target: There is C_d > 0 such that every subgraph A of the box {0,...,n-1}^d with |A| < n^{d/2} satisfies |d_E A| >= C_d |A|^{(d-1)/d}, where d_E A is the edge boundary within the box (so not a case of Theorem 6.22).
detailed_reviews.printed_core: Full proof: choose m maximizing |P_m(A)|; define F = {a in P_m(A): |P_m^{-1}(a)| = n}; observe every a not in F yields at least one edge in d_E A and distinct a give disjoint edges, so |d_E A| >= |P_m(A) \ F|; by Theorem 6.22, |A|^{(d-1)/d} <= prod_j |P_j(A)| <= |P_m(A)|^d; hence |P_m(A)| >= |A|/|A|^{1/d} >= 2^{1/d}|A|/n >= 2^{1/d}|F|; conclude |d_E A| >= (1-2^{-1/d})|P_m(A)| >= (1-2^{-1/d})|A|^{(d-1)/d}.
detailed_reviews.unsupplied_parts: The constant C_d is left as 1-2^{-1/d} at the end; the intermediate inequality |P_m(A)| >= 2^{1/d}|F| and the hypothesis |A| < n^d/2 are printed. Nothing structural is missing.
detailed_reviews.residual_gap: Only the routine choice of C_d absorbing small-n cases is omitted. Recorded glyph conflict: the exercise states |A| < n^{d/2}, the Comment proves under |A| < n^d/2; for n >= 2 the exercise hypothesis is stronger, and the Comment's chain uses |A| < n^d/2 at |P_m(A)| >= |A|/|A|^{1/d} >= 2^{1/d}|A|/n.
detailed_reviews.scope_guards: A is a subgraph of the discrete box; boundary is the edge boundary inside the box; the d_E A notation is the book's.

detailed_reviews.precise_target: G a binary tree. If nu has a tail that decays slower than exponentially, then Phi*_E(G) > 0 yet Phi*_E(G_nu) = 0 a.s., where G_nu is the random subdivision defined in Section 6.9.
detailed_reviews.printed_core: Full proof: non-exponential tail gives, for every c, eps > 0, P[sum_{i<=n} L_i >= c n] >= P[L_1 >= c n] >= e^{-eps n} for infinitely many n, L_i i.i.d. with law nu; take 2^n pairwise disjoint paths from level n to level 2n in the binary tree; P[some path has sum >= c n] >= 1 - (1-e^{-eps n})^{2^n} >= 1 - exp(-e^{-eps n} 2^n) -> 1; with probability -> 1 there is such a path, extend it to the root o, let S be the vertex set of the extended path from o to level 2n; then |d_E S| / sum_{e in E(S)} L_e <= (2n+1)/(c n) ~ 2/c; since c is arbitrary, Phi**_E(G_nu) = 0 a.s. The Phi*_E(G) > 0 half is the standing property of binary trees.
detailed_reviews.unsupplied_parts: None beyond routine bookkeeping: the 'for infinitely many n' quantifier and the a.s. statement are the printed limiting argument, and the constant 2n+1 counts the boundary edges of the extended path.
detailed_reviews.residual_gap: Glyph conflict: the question asks Phi*_E(G_nu) = 0, the Comment's last display concludes Phi**_E(G_nu) = 0. The two expansions differ (Phi**_E <= Phi*_E <= D Phi**_E), so Phi**_E = 0 only gives an upper-bound relation in the wrong direction for deducing Phi*_E = 0 directly; however the printed ratio uses the |E(S)|-normalized denominator and on a single extended path |S| = |E(S)| + 1, so the same displayed bound controls the |S|-normalized ratio as well. Recorded literally; not repaired.
detailed_reviews.scope_guards: Binary tree base graph; nu a subdivision law with slower-than-exponential tail; G_nu the Section 6.9 random subdivision.

h2_family_differences.deciding_printed_evidence: Comment p.638 prints the whole proof: the non-exponential tail gives P[sum_{i<=n} L_i >= c n] >= P[L_1 >= c n] >= e^{-eps n} for infinitely many n; 2^n pairwise disjoint paths from level n to level 2n give P[at least one path has sum >= c n] >= 1 - (1-e^{-eps n})^{2^n} >= 1 - exp(-e^{-eps n} 2^n) -> 1; extending a good path to the root and taking S as the vertex set of the extended path gives |d_E S| / sum_{e in E(S)} L_e <= (2n+1)/(c n) ~ 2/c; since c is arbitrary, the anchored constant vanishes.
h2_family_differences.why_this_is_a_root_difference: Every substantive step is printed, including the counting of the 2^n paths and the ratio bound. The one remaining step is the glyph difference between the question's Phi*_E and the Comment's Phi**_E. The owner's stated link, 'the body inequality Phi**_E <= Phi*_E is the printed link', runs the wrong way for that deduction: Phi**_E = 0 with Phi**_E <= Phi*_E says nothing about Phi*_E. The correct link is also printed, and more directly: body p.238 states that for trees |E(K)| = |K| - 1, 'so Phi**_E(G) = Phi*_E(G) for trees'. Since G is a binary tree, the random subdivision G_nu is again a tree, so the two anchored constants agree exactly and the Comment's conclusion transfers literally. Locally this is the same fact as |S| = |E(S)| + 1 on a single extended path. Either way the gap is a glyph, not mathematics.
